answers.answer: Neither context calls an EHR. Both Post-Round tabs send Copy to EMR through useCopyToEmr, and that calls only copyTextToClipboard: the Capacitor Clipboard on mobile, otherwise navigator.clipboard.writeText, with a hidden-textarea execCommand fallback. A grep of apps/web/src and apps/web/convex for FHIR, HL7, Epic, Cerner, SMART or "EHR" as a whole word finds nothing. In both contexts, marking the encounter complete only saves the app's own record (status set to post-rounded or complete) and writes a usage-analytics row. The in-app export record differs by context. The Hospital tab hands useCopyToEmr a beforeCopy callback that calls logExport("clipboard", 1), so a copy writes the record through api.access.logExport. The Nursing Home tab calls useCopyToEmr(ex.note || "") with no callback, and the file never imports useLogExport, so copying a Nursing Home note writes no export record. The rule says a context without the export record fails. This is a new gap that waits on no open question, so the verdict is fail. I found no "Copy A&P" control in either Post-Round tab, so there was nothing to review for it. The code also predicts problems for the visual layout half: the Nursing Home tab has no Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary card, no Pending Tasks sheet, and its button reads "Mark Visit Complete". A person still has to sign that half off. No recorded gaps or open questions apply.

The verdict is fail. In Hospital Post-Round, Copy to EMR calls useCopyToEmr with a beforeCopy callback, logExport("clipboard", 1). That callback is the api.access.logExport mutation, which writes the in-app export record. The clipboard write then happens through copyTextToClipboard: Capacitor Clipboard on mobile, navigator.clipboard in the browser, or a hidden-textarea execCommand fallback. In Nursing Home Post-Round, Copy calls useCopyToEmr(ex.note || "") with no beforeCopy, and nothing else in that file calls useLogExport. So the Nursing Home Copy only writes to the clipboard and never writes the in-app export record. The pass/fail rule names exactly this case as a fail.

Mark Encounter Complete (Hospital) and Mark Visit Complete (Nursing Home) only save to the app's own record and log an in-app usage event ("note_marked_complete"). They make no outside call.

A case-insensitive grep of apps/web/src and apps/web/convex found no FHIR, HL7, Epic, Cerner, SMART-on-FHIR or EHR identifiers. The static evidence agrees: ehrSource and ehrBundle are both empty. There is no EHR integration.

There is no "Copy A&P" button anywhere in src. The only "A&P" is a template name, so that action cannot be reviewed as written.

No recorded gaps or open questions apply.
